beliefs: f maps every character to the next character in ASCII: ord(ch)+1, with no case folding and no wrapping [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5]
Lowercase letters therefore become uppercase letters (a→B, m→N, y→Z, z→[) [E1, E5]
Uppercase letters become the next uppercase letter or '[' after Z (A→B, Z→[) [E1, E2, E5]
Digits, punctuation, space, and '~' all shift by raw ASCII +1 (0→1, 9→:, space→!, ~→DEL) [E1, E3, E5]
notes: E5 confirms raw ASCII +1 everywhere: lowercase a→B, b→C, y→Z, z→[ (not the lowercase successor). Removed the earlier wrong belief that lowercase maps to next lowercase; the rule is simply ord(ch)+1 for every character.
